name: Governor and Company of the Bank of England
notes: Capital fixed at GBP14,553,000 stock 1816-1946, so value = 0.14553 x price. World No.1 until overtaken by LNWR c.1865-70 (GFD). Nationalisation is outside this era.

name: East India Company (United Company of Merchants of England Trading to the East Indies)
notes: GBP6,000,000 India Stock. Trading monopoly ended 1813 (India) and 1833 (China); from 1834 a fixed 10.5% dividend charged on Indian revenues, so 1834-74 the stock behaved like an annuity. Lost rule of India to the Crown 1858. Stock redeemed at 200 on 30 Apr 1874; company dissolved 1 Jun 1874.

name: Second Bank of the United States
aka: Bank of the United States (Pennsylvania state charter, 1836)
notes: 350,000 shares of $100 ($35m). Federal charter vetoed by Jackson 1832, expired 1836; continued under Pennsylvania charter; suspended 1839 and finally 4 Feb 1841, then liquidated.

name: South Sea Company
notes: Only the trading South Sea Stock is valued (GBP3,662,784 assumed; the annuities were government debt). Stock converted under Gladstone 1853 debt operations; company wound up 1854. Capital figure not verified in this session.

name: London and North Western Railway
notes: Formed 16 Jul 1846 (London & Birmingham + Grand Junction + Manchester & Birmingham). Values use ordinary/consolidated stock only (preference, guaranteed and debenture stocks excluded). Absorbed Lancashire & Yorkshire 1 Jan 1922; into LMS 1 Jan 1923.

name: Midland Railway
notes: Formed 1844. Ordinary stock split 1897 into preferred converted ordinary and deferred converted ordinary; both are included.

name: North Eastern Railway
notes: Formed 1854. Value = North Eastern Consols (ordinary).

name: Great Western Railway
notes: Pre-1880 only the Original stock is captured. Survived the 1923 grouping; nationalised 1948 (outside era).

name: Lancashire and Yorkshire Railway
notes: Merged into LNWR 1 Jan 1922.

name: Compagnie des chemins de fer de Paris a Lyon et a la Mediterranee
notes: 800,000 shares of 500 fr; values use London prices (GBP per share). Merged into SNCF 1938.

name: Compagnie des chemins de fer du Nord
notes: Rothschild railway; 525,000 shares of 400 fr (GBP16). IMM 1890-1913 prints nominal GBP9,274,000 which would imply 579,625 shares: given as est_high. Merged into SNCF 1938.

name: Compagnie du chemin de fer de Paris a Orleans
notes: 600,000 shares of 500 fr (IMM nominal GBP12,000,000). Merged into SNCF 1938.

name: Compagnie des chemins de fer de l'Est
notes: 584,000 shares (IMM nominal GBP11,680,000).

name: Sudbahn-Gesellschaft (Southern Austrian and Lombardo-Venetian Railway)
notes: 750,000 shares of 500 fr. Divided after WWI (1923 reorganised as Danube-Save-Adriatic Railway).

name: East Indian Railway Company
notes: Shares carried a 5% Indian Government guarantee. Purchased by the Government of India from 1 Jan 1880; holders received annuities.

name: Great Indian Peninsula Railway
notes: 5% guaranteed by India. Purchased by the Government of India 1900.

name: Compagnie universelle du canal maritime de Suez
notes: 400,000 shares of 500 fr; amortised capital shares replaced by actions de jouissance. Founders' parts and the parts civiles (Egypt's 15% of profits) are separate securities and NOT included. British government bought 176,602 shares in 1875.

name: Banque de France
notes: Shares: 67,900 (1820s-1848), 91,250 (1848-57), 182,500 (from 1857). Only scattered prices found (Neymarck; JSFS 1884). Nationalised 1945.

name: New York Central Railroad
aka: New York Central & Hudson River RR (1869); New York Central RR (1914)
notes: Largest US company 1860-1880 per GFD. US prices 1862-78 are in greenback dollars.

name: Pennsylvania Railroad
notes: $50 par shares. Largest US company 1912-15 on a common-stock basis (GFD).

name: Union Pacific Railroad
notes: Common + 4% preferred; common-only in note.

name: Great Northern Railway (US)
notes: Its only equity was called preferred stock.

name: Atchison, Topeka and Santa Fe Railway
Standard Oil (Trust 1882; Standard Oil Co. of New Jersey holding company 1899)
notes: About 983,383 shares at dissolution. Not listed on the NYSE before 1920; values from GFD (OTC/curb quotes). Supreme Court ordered dissolution 15 May 1911; subsidiary shares distributed Dec 1911 (GFD dates some trading to Sep 1912; see notes).

name: Standard Oil Company of New York
notes: 1911 spin-off.

name: Standard Oil Company (Indiana)
notes: 1911 spin-off.

name: Standard Oil Company of California
notes: 1911 spin-off.

name: Ohio Oil Company
notes: 1911 spin-off; Hannah value approximate.

name: Prairie Oil & Gas
notes: 1911 spin-off; acquired by Sinclair 1932.

name: Vacuum Oil Company
notes: 1911 spin-off; merged with Socony 1931.

name: Atlantic Refining Company
notes: 1911 spin-off.

name: United States Steel Corporation
notes: 5,083,025 common + 3,602,811 7% preferred shares after 1902-03 (preferred originally $510m, $200m converted into bonds). Values = common + preferred; common-only in note. "First billion-dollar company" refers to par capitalisation incl. bonds (~$1.4bn), not market value.

name: Carnegie Steel Company
notes: Privately held; sale value ~$480m (transaction value).

name: American Telephone and Telegraph Company
notes: Pre-1922 share counts not found in this session (gap).

name: J. & P. Coats
notes: Ordinary only in IMM rows (20% preference excluded).

name: Royal Dutch Petroleum Company (Koninklijke Nederlandsche Petroleum Mij.)
notes: Hannah 1912 figure is for the Royal Dutch/Shell group. 1920/1925 values use the London list share count (2,138,180 x fl100), not verified.

name: "Shell" Transport and Trading Company
notes: 40% partner in the 1907 Royal Dutch/Shell alliance.

name: American Tobacco Company
notes: Broken up Nov 1911; Hannah 1912 value is post break-up.

name: Imperial Tobacco Company (of Great Britain and Ireland)
notes: Largest UK company from 1922/23 (GFD).

name: Fried. Krupp AG
notes: Not publicly traded; Hannah approximation.

name: Hudson's Bay Company
notes: 100,000 shares (GBP17 paid) in the 1870s; small in this era.

name: Anglo-Persian Oil Company
notes: Ordinary shares mostly held by HM Government and Burmah Oil; IMM count may not be total ordinary capital.

name: Courtaulds Ltd
notes: Rayon boom of the 1920s.
